for every $y\in U$. Choose a smooth vector field $N$ on $U$ with

connected component containing $N_y$ in each timelike cone
$\{v\in T_yU:q_y(v,v)<0\}$. Choose an orientation of $U$, and let
$\epsilon_2$ be its metric volume form, characterized by
$\epsilon_2(e_0,e_1)=1$ on every positively oriented $q$-orthonormal frame
with $q(e_0,e_0)=-1$ and $q(e_1,e_1)=1$. Let $r:U\to(0,\infty)$ be smooth.
Take $S^2=\{p\in\mathbb R^3:p\cdot p=1\}$ with the smooth structure and
induced round metric fixed by the earlier dyonic Reissner–Nordström data
definition cited below. Its tangent plane is
$T_pS^2=\{u\in\mathbb R^3:p\cdot u=0\}$, its metric is
$\gamma_{S^2,p}(u,v)=u\cdot v$, and its outward area form is
$(\omega_{S^2})_p(u,v)=\det(p,u,v)$. Write $\wedge$ for the exterior
product of alternating forms. In polar coordinates
$\omega_{S^2}=\sin\theta\,d\theta\wedge d\phi$. Put
$\mathcal M:=U\times S^2$ and define its projections by
$\pi_U(y,p):=y$ and $\pi_S(y,p):=p$. For a smooth map $F:X\to Y$ and a
smooth covariant $2$-tensor field $h$ on $Y$, define its pullback by
$$(F^*h)_x(v,w):=h_{F(x)}(dF_xv,dF_xw),$$
where $x\in X$, $v,w\in T_xX$, and $dF_x:T_xX\to T_{F(x)}Y$ is the
derivative. This formula also defines pullback of a covariant $2$-form.
Define
$$g:=\pi_U^*q+(r\circ\pi_U)^2\pi_S^*\gamma_{S^2}.$$
It has Lorentzian signature $(-,+,+,+)$.
The fibre over $y\in U$ is $S^2_y:=\pi_U^{-1}(\{y\})=\{y\}\times S^2$.
Its induced Riemannian metric is $r(y)^2\gamma_{S^2}$ and its area form is
$r(y)^2\omega_{S^2}$; in polar angles $0<\theta<\pi$ and
$0\le\phi<2\pi$, its area is
$\int_0^{2\pi}\int_0^\pi r(y)^2\sin\theta\,d\theta\,d\phi=4\pi r(y)^2$.
Thus $r(y)>0$ is the areal radius of this orbit sphere.
Choose the four-dimensional orientation so that its metric volume form is
$$\mathrm{vol}_g=-(r\circ\pi_U)^2\,\pi_U^*\epsilon_2\wedge\pi_S^*\omega_{S^2}.$$
In any chart $(x^0,r)$ for which $\epsilon_2=-dx^0\wedge dr$, this gives
$\mathrm{vol}_g=dx^0\wedge dr\wedge r^2\omega_{S^2}$.

diffeomorphism $\rho_R:\mathcal M\to\mathcal M$,
$\rho_R(y,p)=(y,Rp)$, whose inverse is $\rho_{R^{\mathsf T}}$.

$\mathcal M$ is a smooth section of
$$T^a_b\mathcal M:=(T\mathcal M)^{\otimes a}\otimes(T^*\mathcal M)^{\otimes b};$$
at each $x\in\mathcal M$ its value is multilinear on $a$ covectors in
$T_x^*\mathcal M$ and $b$ vectors in $T_x\mathcal M$, where
$T_x^*\mathcal M:=\operatorname{Hom}_{\mathbb R}(T_x\mathcal M,\mathbb R)$.
Smoothness means that the components of the section in every smooth product
chart are $C^\infty$. For such a field $T$, define its pullback by the
diffeomorphism $\rho_R$ by
$$(\rho_R^*T)_x(\alpha_1,\ldots,\alpha_a;v_1,\ldots,v_b)=T_{\rho_R(x)}(\alpha_1\circ(d\rho_R)_x^{-1},\ldots,\alpha_a\circ(d\rho_R)_x^{-1};(d\rho_R)_xv_1,\ldots,(d\rho_R)_xv_b)$$
where $\alpha_i\in T_x^*\mathcal M$, $v_j\in T_x\mathcal M$, and
$(d\rho_R)_x:T_x\mathcal M\to T_{\rho_R(x)}\mathcal M$ is the derivative
of $\rho_R$ at $x$.
A real two-form is a smooth alternating tensor field of type $(0,2)$.
The field $T$ is **rotationally invariant** if $\rho_R^*T=T$ for every
$R\in SO(3)$; a two-form $\mathcal F$ is rotationally invariant in exactly
this sense. This definition specifies a local warped-product model and a
group action. No embedding into a larger spacetime, global potential, maximal
extension, or field equation is assumed.

Let $(M,g,N,o)$ be a smooth oriented, time-oriented Lorentzian four-manifold of signature $(-,+,+,+)$; $o$ is the manifold orientation, $N$ is a smooth future timelike field, and the metric volume form is chosen to agree with $o$. Let $\nabla$ be the metric-selected connection, let $\mathcal F$ be a smooth real two-form on $M$, and use the curvature convention
$R(X,Y)Z=\nabla_X\nabla_YZ-\nabla_Y\nabla_XZ-\nabla_{[X,Y]}Z$.
Define
$$Q_{ab}(\mathcal F):=\mathcal F_{ac}\mathcal F_b{}^c-\frac14 g_{ab}\mathcal F_{cd}\mathcal F^{cd},$$
where both raised indices use $g^{-1}$. A **geometric electrovac datum with zero cosmological constant** is the tuple $(M,g,N,o,\mathcal F)$ satisfying
$$d\mathcal F=0,\qquad d(\star_g\mathcal F)=0,\qquad \operatorname{Ric}_{ab}=2Q_{ab}(\mathcal F)$$
at every point of $M$. Here $\star_g$ is the Lorentzian Hodge map determined by $g$ and $o$; on two-forms $\star_g^2=-1$. No material current, matter tensor, global potential, asymptotic flatness, positive mass, horizon, or extension condition is part of this definition.

For flux integration, an **oriented embedded smooth sphere** means a compact smooth two-dimensional manifold $S$ without boundary, homeomorphic to the unit sphere $\{x\in\mathbb R^3:x\cdot x=1\}$, with a specified orientation in the sense of [[def-oriented-smooth-manifold-and-oriented-chart]] and a smooth inclusion $i:S\hookrightarrow M$. Here smooth embedding means an injective immersion that is a homeomorphism onto its image with the subspace topology ([[def-smooth-embedding]]); identify $S$ with that image. The sphere orientation is specified independently of the spacetime orientation; for coordinate spheres used below it is the stated outward orientation.

For a smooth two-form $\eta$ on a neighborhood of $i(S)$, use the pullback convention of [[def-pullback-of-a-differential-form]],
$$(i^*\eta)_p(v,w)=\eta_{i(p)}(di_pv,di_pw),\qquad p\in S,\quad v,w\in T_pS.$$
By [[prop-pullback-of-forms-is-smooth-functorial-and-preserves-wedges]], this is a smooth top form on $S$. Its support is the closure in $S$ of its nonzero locus ([[def-compactly-supported-differential-form]]), hence is closed in compact $S$ and compact by [[thm-closed-subspace-of-a-compact-space-is-compact]]. Thus $i^*\eta\in\Omega_c^2(S)$.

Write $\mathcal I_S$ for [[def-integral-of-a-compactly-supported-top-form-on-an-oriented-manifold]]: for a subordinate smooth partition $(\rho_j)$ and connected charts $\phi_j$, it sets $\mathcal I_S(\omega)=\sum_j I_{\phi_j}(\rho_j\omega)$, where $I_{\phi_j}$ is the signed chart integral of the compactly supported coefficient. Only finitely many terms are nonzero. The value is independent of charts, partition and refinement by [[thm-global-form-integration-is-independent-of-the-atlas-partition-and-refinement]]. Define the surface notation by
$$\int_S\eta:=\mathcal I_S(i^*\eta).$$
This agrees with [[prop-integration-over-an-oriented-embedded-submanifold]]; a reparametrization here means an orientation-preserving diffeomorphism $F:T\to S$ of oriented smooth two-manifolds (a smooth bijection with smooth inverse and orientation-preserving differential). For such $F$, the same value is $\mathcal I_T((iF)^*\eta)$.
The integration definition and its independence theorem assume $\mathrm{AC}_\omega$, already retained in the geometric background below. For $\eta=\mathcal F$ and $\eta=\star_g\mathcal F$, smoothness of the given field and Hodge map makes both pulled-back top forms admissible; their integrals are finite real numbers. Define the geometric electric and magnetic flux parameters by
$$q_e(S):=\frac1{4\pi}\int_S\star_g\mathcal F,\qquad q_m(S):=\frac1{4\pi}\int_S\mathcal F.$$
When $M$ and the coordinates have length units, these parameters have units of length. A magnetic flux need not have a global potential; no flux quantization is included. The background Lorentzian geometry and Hodge conventions carry the countable-choice assumption $\mathrm{AC}_\omega$ of their named suppliers; the algebraic identities in this definition require no additional choice principle.

The **Axiom of Countable Choice**, written $\mathrm{AC}_\omega$, is the following
statement.

> For every family $(X_n)_{n \in \mathbb{N}}$ of nonempty sets indexed by
> $\mathbb{N}$ there is a function $f$ with domain $\mathbb{N}$ such that
> $f(n) \in X_n$ for every $n \in \mathbb{N}$.

Equivalently, in the vocabulary of Choice function: every at most
countable family of nonempty sets has a choice function.

Fix $p\in S^2$ and put $H_p:=2pp^{\mathsf T}-I_3$. This matrix fixes
$p$ and acts as $-I$ on $p^\perp=T_pS^2$; its eigenvalues are $1,-1,-1$,
so $H_p^{\mathsf T}H_p=I_3$ and $\det H_p=1$, hence $H_p\in SO(3)$. Its
lift fixes $(y,p)$, is the identity on $T_yU$, and is $-I$ on $T_pS^2$. The
decomposition
$\Lambda^2(T_y^*U\oplus T_p^*S^2)=\Lambda^2T_y^*U\oplus
(T_y^*U\otimes T_p^*S^2)\oplus\Lambda^2T_p^*S^2$ is preserved by the
lifted rotation, while the mixed summand changes sign. Invariance therefore
forces the mixed component of $\mathcal F_{(y,p)}$ to equal its negative, so
that component is zero. The first and last summands are one-dimensional,
with generators $\epsilon_2$ and $\omega_{S^2}$. The base form is preserved
because each lift is the identity on $U$, and
$(R^*\omega_{S^2})_p(u,v)=\det(Rp,Ru,Rv)=\det(R)\det(p,u,v)
=\omega_{S^2,p}(u,v)$ for $R\in SO(3)$. To prove transitivity, take
$p,p'\in S^2$,
choose unit vectors $u\perp p$ and $u'\perp p'$, and set $v=p\times u$ and
$v'=p'\times u'$. The oriented orthonormal frames $(p,u,v)$ and $(p',u',v')$
are related by a unique orientation-preserving orthogonal map $R$, which lies
in $SO(3)$ and sends $p$ to $p'$. Thus invariance makes the coefficients of
$\epsilon_2$ and $\omega_{S^2}$ independent of $p$. For a fixed $p_*\in S^2$, the smooth section $j(y):=(y,p_*)$ gives
$j^*\mathcal F=E\epsilon_2$. In any base chart the coefficient of the
nowhere-vanishing smooth form $\epsilon_2$ is nonzero, so division by it
shows that $E$ is smooth locally, hence on $U$. To recover the vertical
coefficient instead, take $p_*=(0,0,1)$, $v=(1,0,0)$ and $w=(0,1,0)$ in
$T_{p_*}S^2$. Along $j$, the product tangent vectors $(0,v)$ and $(0,w)$
are smooth sections of $j^*T\mathcal M$: this follows in any fixed sphere
chart about $p_*$, and requires no frame on all of $S^2$. Smoothness of
$\mathcal F$ therefore makes $y\mapsto\mathcal F_{(y,p_*)}((0,v),(0,w))$
smooth. Since $\omega_{S^2,p_*}(v,w)=\det(p_*,v,w)=1$, this function is
exactly $B(y)$, proving its smoothness. Consequently, uniquely
$\mathcal F=E(y)\epsilon_2+B(y)\omega_{S^2}$.

Since $\epsilon_2$ and $\omega_{S^2}$ are top forms on their respective
two-dimensional factors, their exterior derivatives vanish, and
$d\mathcal F=dB\wedge\omega_{S^2}$. The form $\omega_{S^2}$ never vanishes, so
$d\mathcal F=0$ implies $dB=0$. A smooth function with zero differential is
constant on connected $U$ (differentiate along each smooth path in a
coordinate-ball chain); call this constant $q_m$.

In an oriented orthonormal coframe with $\epsilon_2=-e^0\wedge e^1$ and
$r^2\omega_{S^2}=e^2\wedge e^3$, the four-volume is
$e^0\wedge e^1\wedge e^2\wedge e^3$. The Lorentzian Hodge definition therefore
gives $\star_g\epsilon_2=r^2\omega_{S^2}$ and
$\star_g\omega_{S^2}=-r^{-2}\epsilon_2$. Hence
$\star_g\mathcal F=Er^2\omega_{S^2}-Br^{-2}\epsilon_2$, and
$d(\star_g\mathcal F)=d(Er^2)\wedge\omega_{S^2}$ because a base one-form
wedged with the base top form $\epsilon_2$ vanishes. The second Maxwell equation
implies $d(Er^2)=0$, so $q_e:=Er^2$ is constant on connected $U$. Restricting
$\mathcal F$ and its Hodge dual to $S_y$ gives $q_m\omega_{S^2}$ and
$q_e\omega_{S^2}$; since $\omega_{S^2}=\sin\theta\,d\theta\wedge d\phi$ and
$\int_0^\pi\sin\theta\,d\theta\int_0^{2\pi}d\phi=4\pi$, the stated flux
normalizations follow. This proves existence and uniqueness of both constants.

Let $M$ be a smooth four-manifold without boundary and let $g$ be a smooth
symmetric covariant $2$-tensor field on $M$ such that $g_p$ is nondegenerate at
every $p\in M$ ([[def-gr-smooth-covariant-two-tensor-field]]). Assume
$\mathrm{AC}_\omega$ for the canonical tangent-bundle smooth structure
([[def-countable-choice]], [[def-smooth-vector-field-as-a-tangent-bundle-section]]).
For this general metric define $\flat_p(v):=g_p(v,\cdot)$,
$\sharp_p:=\flat_p^{-1}$, and
$g_p^{-1}(\alpha,\beta):=g_p(\sharp_p\alpha,\sharp_p\beta)$.
Nondegeneracy makes $\flat_p$ injective and hence invertible between the
four-dimensional tangent space and its dual. In a chart, $g^{ab}$ are the
entries of the inverse matrix of $(g_{ab})$. These definitions agree with
[[def-gr-inverse-metric-and-musical-isomorphisms]] in its Lorentzian scope.
Here and below repeated upper/lower indices are summed over $0,1,2,3$.
This holds in particular
when $(M,g,N)$ is a time-oriented smooth Lorentzian four-manifold and $g$ is
its metric ([[def-gr-smooth-lorentzian-objects]]). For smooth local vector fields
$X,Y,Z$ put

$$K(X,Y,Z):=X\bigl(g(Y,Z)\bigr)+Y\bigl(g(Z,X)\bigr)-Z\bigl(g(X,Y)\bigr)+g([X,Y],Z)+g([Z,X],Y)-g([Y,Z],X),$$

with brackets as in [[def-lie-bracket-of-smooth-vector-fields]].

**(a) Existence and formulas.** There is exactly one affine connection
$\nabla$ on $M$ ([[def-affine-connection-on-a-smooth-manifold]]) satisfying

$$2g(\nabla_XY,Z)=K(X,Y,Z)\qquad\text{for all smooth local }X,Y,Z .$$

It is torsion-free and $g$-compatible, so it is a metric-selected connection
for $(M,g)$, meaning torsion-free and satisfying
$Xg(Y,Z)=g(\nabla_XY,Z)+g(Y,\nabla_XZ)$ for smooth local fields
(the conditions of [[def-gr-metric-selected-connection]] extended here to
nondegenerate $g$); in every smooth chart its
Christoffel symbols are

$$\Gamma^a{}_{bc}=\tfrac12\,g^{ad}\bigl(\partial_bg_{dc}+\partial_cg_{bd}-\partial_dg_{bc}\bigr),$$

with $g^{ad}$ the inverse-metric components defined above
([[def-christoffel-symbols-of-an-affine-connection]]).

**(b) Uniqueness.** If an affine connection $\nabla'$ on $M$ is torsion-free
and $g$-compatible, then $\nabla'=\nabla$. Consequently the class
$\operatorname{LC}(M,g)$ of metric-selected connections has exactly one
element; it is the **Levi–Civita connection** of $g$.

$(T_p^*M)^r\times(T_pM)^s\to\mathbb R$
([[def-type-r-s-tensor-on-a-finite-dimensional-vector-space]]); a smooth
tensor field is a section with smooth coefficients in each local product
frame. The empty product is the scalar line. Its chart components are
$T^{a_1\cdots a_r}{}_{b_1\cdots b_s}=T(dx^{a_1},\ldots,dx^{a_r},\partial_{b_1},\ldots,\partial_{b_s})$,
where $dx^a$ is dual to $\partial_a$. This agrees with
[[def-gr-tensor-fields-and-components]] in the Lorentzian case. Put
$T^{a_1\cdots a_r}{}_{b_1\cdots b_s;c}:=(\nabla_{\partial_c}T)^{a_1\cdots a_r}{}_{b_1\cdots b_s}$.

$$T^{a_1\cdots a_r}{}_{b_1\cdots b_s;c}=\partial_cT^{a_1\cdots a_r}{}_{b_1\cdots b_s}+\sum_{i=1}^{r}\Gamma^{a_i}{}_{dc}\,T^{a_1\cdots d\cdots a_r}{}_{b_1\cdots b_s}-\sum_{j=1}^{s}\Gamma^{d}{}_{b_jc}\,T^{a_1\cdots a_r}{}_{b_1\cdots d\cdots b_s},$$

with every contraction in the sense of [[def-contraction-of-a-mixed-tensor]],
and it annihilates the metric and the inverse metric:

$$g_{ab;c}=0,\qquad g^{ab}{}_{;c}=0 .$$

([[def-gr-smooth-lorentzian-objects]]) with metric-selected connection
$\nabla$ ([[def-gr-metric-selected-connection]]), whose existence and
uniqueness are supplied by
[[thm-gr-nondegenerate-levi-civita-and-tensor-derivative]]; that theorem also
extends $\nabla$ to a derivative on tensor fields commuting with contractions
and annihilating $g$ and $g^{-1}$. Let $U\subseteq M$ be open and let
$X,Y,Z$ be smooth vector fields on $U$; brackets are those of
[[def-lie-bracket-of-smooth-vector-fields]], and contractions those of
[[def-contraction-of-a-mixed-tensor]].

assignment

$$R(X,Y)Z:=\nabla_X\nabla_YZ-\nabla_Y\nabla_XZ-\nabla_{[X,Y]}Z .$$

because $\nabla$ is an affine connection

Let $M$ be a smooth four-manifold without boundary and let $g$ be a smooth
symmetric covariant $2$-tensor field on $M$ such that $g_p$ is nondegenerate at
every $p\in M$ ([[def-gr-smooth-covariant-two-tensor-field]]). Assume

([[def-countable-choice]], [[def-smooth-vector-field-as-a-tangent-bundle-section]]).
For this general metric define $\flat_p(v):=g_p(v,\cdot)$,
$\sharp_p:=\flat_p^{-1}$, and
$g_p^{-1}(\alpha,\beta):=g_p(\sharp_p\alpha,\sharp_p\beta)$.
Nondegeneracy makes $\flat_p$ injective and hence invertible between the
four-dimensional tangent space and its dual. In a chart, $g^{ab}$ are the
entries of the inverse matrix of $(g_{ab})$. These definitions agree with
[[def-gr-inverse-metric-and-musical-isomorphisms]] in its Lorentzian scope.
Here and below repeated upper/lower indices are summed over $0,1,2,3$.
This holds in particular
when $(M,g,N)$ is a time-oriented smooth Lorentzian four-manifold and $g$ is

$$K(X,Y,Z):=X\bigl(g(Y,Z)\bigr)+Y\bigl(g(Z,X)\bigr)-Z\bigl(g(X,Y)\bigr)+g([X,Y],Z)+g([Z,X],Y)-g([Y,Z],X),$$

**(a) Existence and formulas.** There is exactly one affine connection
$\nabla$ on $M$ ([[def-affine-connection-on-a-smooth-manifold]]) satisfying

$$2g(\nabla_XY,Z)=K(X,Y,Z)\qquad\text{for all smooth local }X,Y,Z .$$

For smooth vector fields $Y,V$ on an open set $O\subseteq\mathcal M$, define
their Lie bracket on $\varphi\in C^\infty(O)$ by
$[Y,V](\varphi):=Y(V(\varphi))-V(Y(\varphi))$. For a smooth symmetric
covariant $2$-tensor field $h$ on $\mathcal M$ and smooth vector field $Y$,
define its Lie derivative by
$$(\mathcal L_Yh)(V,W):=Y(h(V,W))-h([Y,V],W)-h(V,[Y,W]),$$
for smooth vector fields $V,W$ on a common open set. A vector field is
**Killing** for $h$ when
$\mathcal L_Yh=0$. The quotient coordinate field $\partial_t$
has the product lift $K_{(y,p)}=(\partial_t|_y,0)$ to $\mathcal M$; this
lift is Killing for the full warped metric $g$ and has squared norm $-f$.
Where $f>0$, $K$ is timelike and is future- or past-directed according to the
given time orientation; where $f<0$, $K$ is spacelike and no future/past
designation is asserted. For $\Lambda=0$ this is the dyonic
Reissner–Nordström local form in the stated source convention.
Constant-radius and null-gradient patches, points with $f=0$, global
